objective_for_doctor:
Age: 30
Sex: M
Chief Complaint: shortness of breath

turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?

I’m having significant shortness of breath or difficulty breathing. I also have a cough with colored or more abundant sputum than usual, and a sore throat. My symptoms are more prominent at night. I have COPD and I smoke cigarettes.
Thank you. To help differentiate between a simple COPD exacerbation and a more serious lower respiratory infection, have you had a fever or chills since these symptoms started?
How many days have these worsening symptoms been present?
I don’t know. My symptoms are more prominent at night.
Are you experiencing any chest pain, particularly pain that worsens when you take a deep breath?
Yes— I have pain in the side of the chest (right) and upper chest, and also in the breast (left) and posterior chest wall (left). It’s sensitive and burning.
Does the chest pain worsen when you take a deep breath or cough?
If you press on the areas of your chest that hurt, does the pain get worse?
Do you hear any wheezing or whistling sounds when you breathe?
Do you experience heartburn or a sour/acidic taste in your mouth, particularly when lying down?
Have you used your rescue inhaler (such as albuterol) recently, and did it improve your shortness of breath?

[ABSTAIN] Repeated inability to answer key discriminating questions (symptom duration, presence of fever, response to bronchodilators, pleuritic vs. palpable pain characteristics) prevents confident narrowing of the diagnosis.
[POSSIBLE] Acute COPD exacerbation, Community-acquired pneumonia, Acute bronchitis, Gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD), Musculoskeletal chest wall pain
